wukong.ygen: The Yellow Wind Monster, a yellow marten demon: a lean, sharp-faced demon king with golden fur and a trident, blowing a howling yellow storm of sand from his mouth.
wukong.ygale: The three-sacrifice gale: a towering column of yellow wind tearing across a valley, uprooting trees and blinding soldiers.
wukong.ywind: The yellow wind: a whole landscape swallowed by a churning yellow sandstorm, a pagoda and pines just visible through it.
wukong.eplum: A Plum Mountain brother: one of Erlang Shen's six sworn brothers, a bearded hunter-warrior in green with a bow and a falcon on his arm, among plum blossom.
wukong.ehnd: The howling celestial hound: Erlang Shen's loyal black hunting dog, lean and fierce, leaping with jaws open across a rocky mountain.
wukong.eerl: Erlang Shen, the Illustrious Sage: a handsome, stern god with a third eye blazing on his forehead, in silver armour and a yellow cloak, holding his three-pointed double-edged blade.
wukong.esw: The three-pointed blade: Erlang Shen's long-hafted trident-sword with three double-edged points, flashing as it sweeps through the air. The weapon is the whole picture.
wukong.hnet: The heaven-and-earth net: a vast golden net cast across the sky by heavenly soldiers, falling over a mountain and its forests.
wukong.eye: The third eye: a single vertical eye opening on a god's forehead in extreme close-up, beams of white light shining out and revealing hidden shapes.
wukong.iwnd: A wind spirit: a translucent spirit made of swirling air and leaves, shaped like a dancing girl, spinning over a mountain.
wukong.imaid: A fan maiden: a servant of Princess Iron Fan in green silk, carrying a large palm-leaf fan on her shoulder through the Palm-Leaf Cave.
wukong.iguard: A palm-leaf guard: a stocky guard with a huge round shield shaped like a palm leaf, standing at the gate of Palm-Leaf Cave.
wukong.iprin: Princess Iron Fan, the rakshasa wife of the Bull Demon King, at home in Palm-Leaf Cave: seated on a carved throne in red and gold robes, her giant palm-leaf fan resting across her lap, eyes narrowed and suspicious.
wukong.ifan: The banana-leaf fan: the magical palm-leaf fan alone, as tall as a man, standing upright in a stone hall, its veins glowing faintly. The fan is the whole picture.
wukong.mmon: A shadow monkey: a monkey made entirely of black shadow and smoke, only its glowing eyes clear, slipping along a temple wall.
wukong.mape: A mimic ape: a grey-furred ape with a long face, caught halfway through copying a heavenly soldier standing opposite it; one half of the ape already wears the soldier's gilded armour and plumed helmet, the other half is still bare grey fur. No golden cap, no red cape.
wukong.mear: A listening ear: a macaque crouched on a temple roof with six huge ears fanned out around its head, listening to the whole world, eyes closed.
wukong.mac6: The six-eared macaque, the false Great Sage: a dark-furred imposter of the Monkey King with six pointed ears, in black armour and a dark cap, his staff dark iron, standing in front of a mirror where his reflection is golden; cold and sinister.
wukong.mecho: The echo of the staff: two iron staffs, one solid black iron and one a pale ghostly copy of it, crashing down side by side onto a stone floor at the same instant, two rings of shockwave and ink-splash crossing. Only the two staffs and the impact, no one holding them.
wukong.mtrump: The second self: two identical figures standing back to back, one in light and one in shadow, joined by a thread of smoke, on an empty stage.
wukong.bgrd: A bull guard: a hulking bull-headed demon in iron armour with a huge iron club, nostrils steaming.
wukong.bcap: A buffalo captain: a water-buffalo demon officer with curved horns and a heavy halberd, riding a war cart.
wukong.bhrn: A horned vanguard: a bull demon charging head-down with its great horns lowered, dust exploding behind it.
wukong.bdk: The Bull Demon King, sworn brother turned enemy of the Monkey King: a colossal demon king with a black bull's head and huge horns, in black and gold armour, gripping a mixed-iron cudgel, his eyes burning red.
wukong.bfury: The fury of the bull: a vast white bull of smoke and fire rearing over a burning mountain, its horns scraping the clouds.
wukong.pdis: A stone disciple: a stone statue of a monk on a mountain path slowly coming to life, cracks of golden light in its body, eyes opening.
wukong.pfin: A finger of the mountain: a single colossal stone pillar shaped like a finger rising from the clouds, carved with sutras.
wukong.pgrd: A mountain warden: a stone guardian lion-dog on a temple step, its stone mane cracked and mossy, its eyes glowing gold.
wukong.plm: The Buddha's palm: the serene Tathagata Buddha seen from far below, seated on a lotus among clouds, his right hand raised in the gesture of blessing, golden light pouring from his palm.
wukong.palm: The five-finger mountain: five immense peaks shaped like fingers standing in a ring in a sea of clouds, a golden talisman fluttering at the summit of the tallest.
wukong.karma: Divine Karma, the cosmic ledger of merit: a giant celestial abacus of glowing jade beads floating among auspicious clouds, the beads sliding by themselves to count good and bad deeds, a golden thread of merit carrying a few beads over to the next row.
wukong.dint: Divine intervention: a vast radiant golden hand reaching down out of curling auspicious clouds to catch a falling, wounded warrior just before he strikes the mountainside, lotus petals drifting down around it.

thoth.dosir: Osiris, lord of the dead: the green-skinned king of the underworld seated on his throne, wrapped in white linen like a mummy, wearing the tall white atef crown with two ostrich plumes, holding the crook and flail crossed over his chest, a lake of lotus flowers at his feet.
thoth.gweigh: The weighing of the heart: the great golden scales of judgement in the Hall of Two Truths, a human heart on one pan and the white feather of Ma'at on the other, perfectly balanced; the jackal-headed Anubis kneeling to steady the scale and the monster Ammit, part crocodile, part lion, part hippo, waiting below.
thoth.ithoth: The Book of Thoth, the forbidden book of all magic: a golden box inside a box of ivory and ebony, inside a box of silver, opened at last in a dark tomb, the papyrus scroll within glowing so brightly that the light pours out like water.
thoth.iseshat: Seshat, mistress of books and goddess of writing: a woman in a leopard-skin robe with a seven-pointed star crowned by a bow on her head, writing on a long palm rib with a reed pen, measuring cords coiled at her side, in a temple library lined with scroll niches.
thoth.yibis: An ibis of Thoth: a sacred white ibis with black head and long curved beak wading in the shallows of the Nile among papyrus reeds, one foot raised, the reflection of a crescent moon in the water.
thoth.ybab: A baboon of the dawn: a sacred baboon sitting on a temple pylon with its arms raised to greet the rising sun, a crescent moon and disc on its head, the sun's first rays striking its fur.
thoth.dembal: An embalmer: a priest in a jackal mask of Anubis bending over a body wrapped in linen on a lion-shaped embalming table, holding a jar of resin and a strip of linen, canopic jars lined up beside him.
thoth.tscar: A scarab amulet: a single large carved scarab of lapis lazuli and gold with outspread falcon wings, resting on folded white linen, glowing faintly. The amulet is the whole picture.
thoth.iweret: Weret-Hekau, Great of Magic: a lioness-headed goddess with a sun disc and cobra on her head, rearing up with arms spread as magic crackles between her hands, protective serpent amulets coiling in the air around her.
thoth.yall: The All-Seeing Scribe: Thoth himself, the ibis-headed god in a white kilt and broad collar, seated cross-legged with a reed pen and a scribe's palette, writing on a papyrus that stretches up into the sky, every deed of gods and men appearing on it as it unrolls.
thoth.ysenet: Senet with the Moon: Thoth playing the board game senet against Khonsu, the moon god, on a moonlit temple roof, winning five extra days of light from the moon; the glowing moon disc above, the board between them, the game pieces shining.
thoth.dammit: The devouring jaws: Ammit, the devourer of the dead, part crocodile, part lion and part hippopotamus, lunging forward with her crocodile jaws wide open to swallow a heart that has failed the judgement.
thoth.ykhon: Khonsu, the moon-traveller: a young god with the sidelock of youth and a crescent moon cradling a full moon disc on his head, wrapped like a mummy and holding a crook and flail, travelling across the night sky in a silver boat.
thoth.dmum: A mummy of the Old Kingdom: an ancient royal mummy in faded linen and a cracked gold mask, rising from its stone sarcophagus in a dusty tomb, its painted eyes glowing.
thoth.ieye: The Eye of Horus, the wedjat: a huge golden-and-lapis wedjat-eye amulet floating in the air, its painted eye opening and looking out, rays of light spreading from it. The eye is the whole picture.
thoth.dduat: The gate of the Duat: one of the twelve fiery gates of the underworld, a tall pylon guarded by a great serpent coiled along the top and fire-breathing cobras at its doors, the boat of the sun waiting in the dark river before it.
thoth.tmedj: A Medjay of the temple: a tall, lean desert warrior in a white kilt and red sash with an ostrich-feather in his hair, a bow over his shoulder and a long spear, guarding a temple doorway.
thoth.tscr: A temple scribe: a young scribe sitting cross-legged in the classic pose with a papyrus roll across his kilt, a reed pen behind his ear, ink palette at his side, in a sunlit courtyard.
thoth.dbal: A soul-bird keeper: an old priest gently holding a Ba-bird, a small falcon with a human head, on his wrist in a tomb chapel lit by lamps.
thoth.dnomad: A wandering Ba: a little human-headed bird soul flying out of a tomb shaft into the evening sky over the desert, looking back at the tomb.
thoth.ichisel: A chisel: a sculptor's copper chisel and wooden mallet chipping a name out of a carved stone relief, chips of stone flying.
thoth.iwas: A was-sceptre: the long sceptre of power with its animal-head top and forked base, standing upright in a ray of light before an altar. The sceptre is the whole picture.
thoth.tpen: A reed pen: a scribe's reed pen dipped in black ink, the ink trail it leaves on papyrus lifting off the page and turning into a flying bird.
thoth.gnile: The gift of the Nile: the river in flood, green fields and palm trees on its banks, a fisherman's papyrus boat and a crocodile in the shallows, the god Hapi pouring water from jars.
thoth.gcanop: Canopic jars: the four canopic jars of alabaster with lids shaped as the heads of a man, a baboon, a jackal and a falcon, standing in a row in a painted chest.
thoth.ystar: A star-reader: a priest-astronomer on a temple roof at night holding a merkhet sighting tool up to the stars, the sky full of the constellations of Egyptian astronomy.
thoth.ywatch: A watcher at the gate: a stern gatekeeper demon of the underworld with a knife in each hand and the head of a ram, sitting before a closed door in the Duat.
thoth.dheart: A heart scarab: a large green stone scarab carved with a spell on its underside, set into a gold frame on the chest of a mummy, glowing faintly.
thoth.tsun: Sunder the soul: a priest raising an ostrich-feather fan over a dying warrior as his soul parts in two, the Ka rising as a pale double of his body with raised arms on its head, the Ba flying free as a human-headed bird.
thoth.dsk: A Ka-keeper: a priestess tending a row of painted Ka statues in a tomb's statue chamber, offering bread and beer, each statue with the raised-arms Ka sign on its head.
thoth.dcut: A ritual knife: a curved flint ritual knife with a gold handle lying on an alabaster offering table beside lotus flowers and a bowl. The knife is the whole picture.
thoth.dpart: The parting of souls: a pale ghostly double stepping out of a sleeping man's body in a dim tomb, a small human-headed bird hovering above them.
thoth.dwrap: Linen wrappings: long strips of fine white linen unrolling through the air around a mummy shape, amulets tucked between the layers glinting.
thoth.dreun: Reunion in the Field of Reeds: a man and his Ba-bird reunited in the paradise of the Field of Reeds, ploughing golden wheat beside blue canals under a perfect sky.
thoth.dsever: Sever the mighty: a giant enemy warrior's great shadow being cut away from his body by a priest's knife of light, the warrior staggering.
thoth.dshade: Sheut, the shadow: a long black shadow-soul stretching across a sunlit temple floor, standing up on its own and walking away from the body that cast it.
thoth.dcart: A cartouche ring: a gold ring shaped as a royal cartouche, an oval with a loop of rope, set with carnelian and turquoise, resting on a cushion. The ring is the whole picture.
thoth.dtwof: The amulet of the two feathers: a gold amulet of two tall plumes standing side by side, set with lapis and turquoise inlay, catching the desert light.
thoth.dweigh: A weigher of souls: an assessor of the dead, a stern god with a feather on his head sitting in judgement, holding up a small set of golden scales.
thoth.dkhep: Khepri's rebirth: the scarab god Khepri, a great golden scarab beetle, rolling the newborn red sun up over the eastern horizon at dawn.
thoth.dakh: Akh, the glorified: a reunited soul shining with light like a star, a figure of radiant gold rising from a tomb into the sky, the Ka and Ba merging into it.
thoth.dsplit: The scattering of the pieces: fragments of a broken statue of a king flying apart in a burst of dust and light, its pieces scattering across the desert.
thoth.dren: Names of the dead: rows of carved royal cartouches on a dark tomb wall glowing gold one by one as a priest's lamp passes over them.
thoth.dsoul: A soul-collector: a gaunt priest in a black panther skin walking through a desert necropolis at dusk with a net full of fluttering human-headed Ba-birds.
thoth.dbook: The Book of Gates: a long painted papyrus unrolled across a tomb floor, showing the night journey of the sun boat through the twelve gates of the underworld, glowing serpents guarding each gate.
thoth.iink: The ink of Seshat: a scribe's palette with cakes of red and black ink, a reed pen dipping in, the ink rising from the palette in a glowing curl.
thoth.iscribe: An apprentice scribe: a boy with the sidelock of youth practising hieroglyphs on a limestone flake, tongue between his teeth in concentration, an older scribe watching.
thoth.iword: The amulet of words: a small lapis-and-gold amulet shaped like a papyrus roll on a cord, glowing faintly, lying on an open scroll.
thoth.iglyph: A glyph-warded guard: a temple guard in a white kilt with a tall spear and shield, protective symbols painted in red on his chest and arms glowing faintly.
thoth.itut: A tutor of scribes: an elderly scribe teacher with a cane in a shaded schoolroom courtyard, boys copying texts on boards in front of him.
thoth.isac: Sacred text: a priest reading aloud from a long papyrus scroll in a dark sanctuary, the words he speaks rising from the page as a stream of golden light.
thoth.iliv: A living papyrus: a long papyrus scroll that has come alive, rising and twisting like a serpent, its painted figures stepping out of its surface.
thoth.ierase: Damnatio, the erasure: a wall relief of a pharaoh whose face and name have been chiselled away, the stone fresh and raw where the image used to be.
thoth.ishen: The shen ring: a gold shen ring, a circle of rope with a straight bar at the bottom, held in the talons of a falcon with outspread wings.
thoth.idjed: The djed pillar: a tall pillar of stacked bands, the backbone of Osiris, raised upright by priests with ropes in a temple ceremony.
thoth.ikhem: The keeper of sacred texts: an old priest in a leopard skin standing before tall niches stacked with papyrus rolls in the House of Life, a single lamp in his hand.
thoth.iunwr: Unwriting: painted hieroglyphs lifting off an open papyrus scroll and dissolving back into drifting droplets of black and red ink in the air above it. Only the scroll and the dissolving signs, no person and no god.
thoth.ihekau: Words of heka, words of power: a magician-priest with arms raised speaking a spell, golden glyph-shapes of power streaming from his mouth and swirling around a war chariot.
thoth.iobel: The obelisk of words: a towering red granite obelisk with a gold-capped top catching the first sun, standing before a temple pylon, tiny people at its base for scale.
thoth.ianx: The ankh of life: a large golden ankh glowing with life, held out by a god's hand toward the lips of a kneeling pharaoh. The ankh is the focus.
thoth.inarm: The palette of Narmer: the great carved stone ceremonial palette of the first king, standing in a pool of light, its relief showing the king striking his enemy.
thoth.iname: The unspoken name: an empty golden cartouche, an oval ring of rope with nothing written inside, glowing alone in total darkness in a sealed tomb chamber, a single shaft of light falling on it. No person and no god.
thoth.yread: Read the signs: a priest watching a flock of birds wheel across the sunset sky over the Nile, reading their pattern as an omen.
thoth.yclerk: A temple archivist: a scribe in a vast archive room climbing a ladder to reach a jar of rolled papyri on a high shelf, lamp in hand.
thoth.ywarn: Forewarned: a sentry on a desert fort's wall shading his eyes and pointing at dust rising on the horizon, a horn at his lips.
thoth.yledger: A ledger of deeds: a wide view of a royal granary courtyard at harvest, workers carrying sacks and pouring grain into heaps while a scribe sits small in the shade recording the count, cattle and carts beyond.
thoth.yprep: Lay the snare: hunters in a papyrus marsh stretching a clap-net between the reeds, waiting for a flock of ducks to land.
thoth.ypre: Preempt: a hand closing a temple door just as an enemy's spear-point thrusts through the gap, catching it.
thoth.yrecall: Recorded history: a long wall relief of a famous battle with chariots and archers, its painted figures faintly coming alive and stepping off the wall.
thoth.ysage: A sage of Hermopolis: an old, wise priest of the city of Thoth sitting beneath a palm tree with a sacred ibis beside him, teaching from a scroll.
thoth.yfore: Foreknowledge: an oracle priestess in a dark shrine gazing into a bowl of oil and water, a vision of the future glowing on its surface.
thoth.ycopy: A scribe's copy: seen from directly above, two identical papyrus scrolls lying side by side on a reed mat with ink cakes, brushes and a water pot, only a scribe's two hands visible as one copies the last line.
thoth.ytrap: Ambush foretold: archers hidden among desert rocks with bows drawn, waiting as an enemy chariot approaches below, unaware.
thoth.yhall: The hall of records: a vast hypostyle hall of painted columns, every column covered in records, lit by shafts of light from the high windows.
thoth.ycount: Countermeasure: two war chariots meeting head-on in the desert, one charioteer raising a shield that catches every arrow aimed at him.
thoth.yvizier: The vizier's report: the vizier, a dignified official in a long white robe and a gold collar, kneeling before the throne to read a report from a scroll.
thoth.yechoes: Echoes of the past: ghostly faded copies of an ancient army marching across the desert through the heat haze, their outlines flickering.
thoth.yjudge: A judge of words: a stern judge in a long robe with the feather of Ma'at pinned to his collar, pointing a finger at an accused man in a courtroom of columns.
thoth.ytruth: Ma'at's ledger: the goddess Ma'at, a woman with a tall ostrich feather on her headband and outspread winged arms, kneeling over an open book of truth that glows gold.
thoth.gscroll: A scroll of protection: a small papyrus scroll of spells rolled and tied with red thread, glowing as it shields a sleeping child from shadowy demons at the edge of the room.
thoth.gfeather: The feather of Ma'at: a single tall white ostrich feather standing upright on a gold base, radiating calm light. The feather is the whole picture.
thoth.gpriest: A priest of Thoth: a shaven-headed priest in white linen with a panther skin over one shoulder, carrying a small statue of an ibis in procession.
thoth.karma: Divine Karma in Egypt: the great ledger of the gods, an immense open papyrus book resting on the back of a sacred baboon of Thoth, every deed written in it glowing, a few glowing signs floating up off the page to be carried forward.
thoth.dint: Divine intervention: a vast radiant golden hand reaching down from a blazing winged sun disc in the sky to catch a falling, wounded warrior just before he strikes the desert sand.
thoth.grob: A grave robber: a wiry thief in a dusty loincloth and headcloth prising the gold mask off a mummy by the light of a single oil lamp, glancing nervously over his shoulder.
thoth.tdig: A tunnel digger: a sweating robber chipping through the stone of a tomb wall with a copper chisel, rubble around his knees, a rope leading back up a narrow shaft.
thoth.fence: A black-market fence: a sly merchant in a dim market stall weighing stolen gold amulets on a small balance, a curtain half hiding crates of grave goods.
thoth.mthief: The master of thieves: a confident, scarred robber chief lounging on a pile of stolen treasure in a hidden cave, a gold collar on his neck, tossing a ring in his hand.
thoth.torch: Torchlight: a burning reed torch thrust into a dark tomb corridor, its light falling on painted walls and startling a nest of bats.
thoth.drag: Drag below: a hand reaching out of a dark tomb shaft to grab a guard's ankle and pull him down into the blackness.
thoth.trob: Grave-goods: a robbed tomb chamber heaped with gilded chairs, chests, chariots and statues, a robbers' rope hanging down through a hole in the ceiling.
thoth.sbrood: A scorpion brood: a swarm of small black scorpions pouring out from under a cracked stone slab in the desert, tails raised.
thoth.sstalk: A sand stalker: a huge pale desert scorpion half buried in the sand, only its pincers and raised stinger showing as it waits.
thoth.squeen: Serket's handmaiden: a priestess of the scorpion goddess with a scorpion crown, live scorpions crawling harmlessly over her arms as she raises a bowl of venom.
thoth.sking: The scorpion king: a fierce early king of Egypt in the white crown with a scorpion emblem on his standard, raising a ceremonial mace before his army.
thoth.sting: The sting of Serket: a giant scorpion's tail curling down and striking, venom glistening at its tip. The sting is the whole picture.
thoth.curse2: The curse of the pharaoh: a tomb robber recoiling in terror as a sealed tomb door bursts open, a cold wind and glowing eyes rushing out of the dark.
thoth.serk: Serket's venom: the goddess Serket with a scorpion on her head, holding up a glowing cup of venom, scorpions circling her feet.
thoth.shbs: A shabti servant: a small blue faience shabti figurine with a hoe and basket coming to life in a tomb, stepping off its shelf among rows of others.
thoth.mumw: A tomb mummy: a wrapped mummy shuffling out of a dark burial chamber, linen strips trailing, one arm reaching forward.
thoth.embp: An embalming priest: an old priest with a jar of natron salt and a bundle of linen in the House of Purification, preparing a body on a stone table.
thoth.tguard: The mummy king: a mummified pharaoh in a crumbling gold-trimmed shroud and the double crown, standing in his burial chamber with a crook and flail, his painted eyes glowing.
thoth.heal2: The waters of the Nile: a priest pouring water from a tall silver jar over a wounded warrior on the riverbank, the water glowing with healing light.
thoth.shab: The shabti oath: hundreds of small shabti figures standing in ranks in a tomb, all raising their hoes together as if answering a call.
thoth.croc: A Nile crocodile: a huge crocodile bursting out of the river shallows with its jaws wide open, water and spray flying.
thoth.lurk: A Nile lurker: only the eyes and snout of a crocodile showing above the green water among papyrus reeds, ripples spreading.
thoth.sobpr: A priest of Sobek: a priest feeding a sacred crocodile adorned with gold earrings and bracelets in a temple pool.
thoth.sobek: Sobek, lord of the waters: the crocodile-headed god in a gold collar and kilt, a sun disc and plumes on his head, rising from the Nile with a was-sceptre.
thoth.sobk: The jaws of Sobek: the enormous open jaws of a crocodile seen from inside, framing a boat on the river beyond.
thoth.jack: A desert jackal: a lean golden jackal trotting across the dunes at dusk, ears pricked, looking back over its shoulder.
thoth.jguard: A jackal guard: a black jackal lying watchful on top of a shrine chest, like the statue of Anubis in a tomb, eyes gleaming.
thoth.wepw: Wepwawet, the opener of ways: the wolf-headed god in white and gold standing on a standard at the front of an army, a mace and a bow in his hands, the desert road opening ahead.
thoth.jpack: A jackal packleader: a big black jackal leading a pack down a desert ridge at night, the others' eyes glowing behind it.
thoth.anub: The guides of the dead: Anubis, the jackal-headed god, leading a newly dead soul by the hand through the dark of the underworld toward a distant light.
thoth.hekp: A priest of Heka: a priest with a shaven head holding a pair of serpent-shaped magic wands, speaking a spell over a sick child.
thoth.snake: A temple cobra: a rearing cobra with its hood spread, coiled on a temple altar beside offerings of bread and fruit.
thoth.hekmag: A magician of the court: a court magician performing before the pharaoh, turning his staff into a living serpent on the palace floor.
thoth.hekhigh: The high priest of Heka: an imposing high priest in a leopard skin and gold collar raising an ivory magic wand carved with protective creatures, light swirling around it.
thoth.heka: Execration: a priest smashing red clay pots inscribed with the names of enemies, the shards flying and dark smoke rising from them.
thoth.ammit: Ammit the devourer prowling the Hall of Judgement: the beast with a crocodile's head, a lion's forequarters and a hippo's hindquarters pacing beside the great scales, licking her jaws.
thoth.soulw: A wailing soul: a pale, translucent dead spirit with its hands to its face, wailing in the grey mist of the underworld.
thoth.unwor: The unworthy dead: a line of ghostly souls whose hearts were heavier than the feather, cast into a lake of fire in the underworld.
thoth.hguard2: The guardian of the scales: a huge baboon of Thoth seated on top of the beam of the great scales of judgement, watching the balance.
thoth.ammt: Devour the unworthy: a heart falling from the pan of the scales into the open jaws of a crocodile-headed beast below.
thoth.sphinx2: The Great Sphinx: the colossal lion-bodied sphinx with a pharaoh's head lying before the pyramids at Giza, its eyes slowly opening as if waking.
thoth.sphg: A sphinx guardian: one of a long avenue of ram-headed sphinx statues lining the approach to a temple, the nearest one turning its head.
thoth.sphs: A desert sentinel: a winged sphinx standing guard on a rocky outcrop above the desert, wings half spread, watching the horizon.
thoth.sphx: The riddle of the sphinx: a traveller standing small before a great sphinx at night under the stars, the sphinx leaning down to speak.
thoth.apepx: Apophis, the serpent of chaos: an enormous coiling serpent rising out of the dark waters of the underworld to swallow the sun boat of Ra, its mouth wide.
thoth.apsp: A spawn of Apophis: a black serpent with red eyes slithering out of a crack in the earth, smoke curling around it.
thoth.apcoil: A chaos coil: the huge coils of a serpent wrapping around a toppled temple column, crushing the stone.
thoth.sand: A sandstorm: a towering wall of red-brown sand rolling across the desert toward a caravan, swallowing the sky.
thoth.apep: The unmaking: the cat of Ra slicing the head off the serpent Apophis with a knife beneath the sacred persea tree, the serpent's coils thrashing.
thoth.setg: Set, lord of the red desert: the god with the head of a strange curved-snouted beast and tall square ears, in red and gold, holding a was-sceptre in a howling desert storm.
thoth.setb: The beast of Set: a lean dog-like animal with a curved snout, tall square-topped ears and a forked tail, prowling the red desert.
thoth.setst: A storm of the desert: a black thundercloud of sand and lightning sweeping over the red desert, a beast-shaped head faintly visible in the storm.
thoth.setx: The dismemberment: the coffin of Osiris floating down the Nile at night, Set's shadow looming over it on the riverbank.
thoth.sekhg: Sekhmet, the eye of Ra: the lioness-headed goddess of war in a red dress with a sun disc and cobra on her head, roaring with flames streaming from her mouth across the desert.
thoth.lion: A lioness of Sekhmet: a powerful lioness charging across the desert in the red light of sunset, sand flying from her paws.
thoth.plague: A bringer of plague: a dark messenger of Sekhmet with a lion's mask and a quiver of glowing arrows, loosing them over a city at night.
thoth.sekh: The eye of Ra: a huge blazing eye of fire in the sky, a lioness's shape inside the flames, scorching the desert below.
